vision.title: The Adventure Begins

inputs.title: The Adventure Begins
inputs.logline: When eager young Keen sails away from home and into a storm, he discovers that courage is not looking fearless — it is hearing someone else need him, feeling the gulp, and going anyway.

orderedEvents.text: Tall flowers sway gently in the warm breeze. Some stretch high above the grass, with long soft necks and bright open petals full of pollen. FUZZBY and ZENNY weave between them collecting pollen from flower to flower. Fine golden pollen dusts their paws and trails softly through the air. Zenny works with smooth calm precision — neat, efficient, graceful. Fuzzby does not. He zig-zags wildly through the air, humming loudly to himself as he works.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…
He dips low into a flower, scoops up pollen — then overdoes it and spins sideways into a leaf. FWIP. He bounces back into the air and straightens up proudly.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: Nailed it.
Zenny glides up beside him. Watches him for a beat.

beats.storyBeat: The episode opens at bee scale in a bright flower field: Zenny’s graceful competence and Fuzzby’s chaotic overconfidence are instantly legible. Fuzzby’s first pollen dive becomes a crash he rebrands as mastery, planting the whole episode’s comic idea that bravado is not the same as courage.
beats.want: Fuzzby wants to collect pollen like an impressive professional and be seen doing it.
beats.need: He needs to know he belongs even when his body betrays his grand self-image.
beats.kidRead: Funny bee zooms too fast, hits a leaf, bounces back and pretends he meant it.
beats.adultRead: A tiny performer is already covering embarrassment with status — lovable because the mask is transparent.
beats.emotionalIntent: Start with easy laughter, high energy and immediate character contrast, with no danger yet beyond Fuzzby’s own momentum.

beats.need: He needs to stop treating every mistake as something to hide.

beats.need: He needs permission to be unsure and still go.
beats.kidRead: Keen packs and checks and checks again before sailing away.
beats.adultRead: A child is performing independence in front of a parent who can see every crack and chooses not to crush it.
beats.emotionalIntent: Make the goodbye ordinary and tactile before it becomes ceremonial.

vision.premise: Keen leaves his Mum and the safety of home, sails into weather bigger than he expected, saves Squeaky before he has any crystal power, and is welcomed into the Crystal Bears when the courage already inside him finds its visible form.
vision.dramaticQuestion: Can Keen stop performing bravery long enough to discover the real thing — acting through fear for someone who needs him?
vision.theme: Courage is not the absence of fear; it is the scared part and the brave part moving together.
vision.externalJourney: Keen packs a small sailboat, says goodbye at the pier, meets Squeaky, gets lost in a storm, follows Squeaky toward help, dives underwater to free him from a net, reaches Crystal Cove, receives the Aquamarine in his father’s wristbands, and walks into his new family.
vision.internalJourney: Keen begins trying to prove he is ready and fearless, keeps covering wobble with confidence, meets his real valley when the storm strips away map, boat and certainty, then acts without hesitation for Squeaky and learns that the fear he felt did not cancel his courage — it made the courage real.
vision.relationshipChanges: Keen and his Mum move from close protection to trusted distance through the wristbands. Keen and Squeaky become friends through play, danger, rescue and mutual rescue. Aida moves from distant witness to welcomer, completing Mum’s act of letting go with a found-family welcome. Fuzzby shifts from comic self-importance to genuine awe of Keen.
vision.emotionalCurve: Warm morning play and goodbye, then comic buoyancy, then cooling uncertainty, storm panic, the underwater nadir with one charged wordless wristband beat, explosive relief, soft welcome, ceremonial belonging, and a golden-hour laugh that still remembers the boat and the goodbye.
vision.comedyCurve: Fuzzby’s proud-bumbler pollen escalation opens the episode, then Keen inherits the same cover-up grammar in his wobble and map confusion. As danger rises, comedy narrows into release valves — Fuzzby’s emergency crashes, Zenny’s dry precision, the dolphin-cowboy ride — before ending with Fuzzby’s honey-friendship overcommitment.
vision.setupPayoffMap: Fuzzby’s 'Nailed it' cover-up sets the comic grammar for Keen’s 'Still got it.' Mum’s vacant wristbands are handed over with no glow, then self-glow underwater when Keen finds courage from within, then receive Aquamarine gems in the ceremony. Aida’s bowl vision of pier, boat and Mum pays off in her timely rescue beacon and later message home. Squeaky’s playful chatter pays off as urgent signaling in the storm and mutual rescue at the surface.
vision.visualMotifs: Empty gold wristbands becoming faint aqua, then crystal-set azure; small figures against wide water; paws closing around objects of trust; warm home receding into distance; storm-grey swallowing horizon; rose-pink beacon cutting through rain; wet sand and droplets after cost; final golden beach path with the group moving as one.
vision.sonicMotifs: Fuzzby’s manic buzz-crash rhythm; Zenny’s dry stillness after chaos; Aida’s low bowl tone blooming into rose light; Keen’s repeated self-steadying phrase; Squeaky’s chirps shifting from play to distress to relief; Aquamarine’s B-note emerging from muffled underwater hush into the group chord.
vision.climax: Underwater, with Squeaky tangled and the massive wave gathering, Keen sees his father’s vacant wristbands faintly glow, centers himself, pulls with everything he has, tears the net free, is thrown by the wave, and is then carried back up by the friend he saved.
vision.resolution: Aida awards Keen the Aquamarine, the crystal splits into two gems that settle into his father’s wristbands, the group swamps him in a hug, and the phrase from Mum’s goodbye returns as a found-family truth: wherever he goes, he will not be alone.
vision.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, buoyant belonging with a visible trace of cost — the storm has passed and everyone laughs, but Keen’s boat is gone, Mum had to let him go, and the wristbands carry both loss and home.

orderedEvents.text: Tall flowers sway gently in the warm breeze. Some stretch high above the grass, with long soft necks and bright open petals full of pollen. FUZZBY and ZENNY weave between them collecting pollen from flower to flower. Fine golden pollen dusts their paws and trails softly through the air. Zenny works with smooth calm precision — neat, efficient, graceful. Fuzzby does not. He zig-zags wildly through the air, humming loudly to himself as he works.

He dips low into a flower, scoops up pollen — then overdoes it and spins sideways into a leaf. FWIP. He bounces back into the air and straightens up proudly.

orderedEvents.text: Nailed it.
Zenny glides up beside him. Watches him for a beat.

beats.storyBeat: The episode opens at bee scale in a bright flower field: Zenny’s graceful competence and Fuzzby’s chaotic overconfidence are instantly legible. beats.adultRead: A tiny performer is already covering embarrassment with status — lovable because the mask is transparent.

treatments.name: Treatment 1 — Fuzzby’s Grand Flight That the World Keeps Correcting
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience is launched into the scene inside Fuzzby’s certainty: fast, bright, overconfident and a little too close to the next mistake. Children feel the fun of zooming through giant flowers; adults see the tiny performer working very hard to look important. The scene starts as pure play, then lets the first thundercloud shave a little warmth off the laughter without stopping the comedy.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Fuzzby’s want governs the scene: he wants to be impressive at pollen collecting, then official, then unbothered by pressure. His need stays underneath: to be allowed to belong even when the evidence says he is a disaster. Zenny is not the emotional centre; she is the calm witness who sees through the performance and stays near anyway.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary mechanism: escalating overcommitment. Every Fuzzby correction worsens the confession — the efficient pollen dive becomes a leaf bounce, the proud recovery becomes a pollen moustache, the attempt to fix the moustache becomes a bigger smear, the chain reaction becomes “Buzz Crash!!”, and the pressure boast becomes immediate flower imprisonment. Secondary mechanism: hiding failure. “Nailed it.” and “Good thing I work well under pressure.” are funny because his body has already disproved them.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Fuzzby is all intention and momentum: chest forward, wings overworking, altitude porpoising, turns too sharp for his own body. He never simply bumps; each crash is the consequence of trying to look masterful one fraction too hard. His pride resets faster than his balance, so he is still physically recovering while verbally claiming victory. Zenny moves with small, efficient decisions: one clean glide, one exact pollen scoop, one held look. Her affection is in staying close enough to catch the next nonsense, not in softening the tease.
treatments.visualGrammar: The flower field is enormous at bee scale, with stems as pillars and petals as high platforms. The visual grammar favours rushing diagonals, sudden near-misses, pollen streaks in depth and frame edges that Fuzzby nearly outruns. Zenny’s appearances are composed as calm interruptions: the world briefly stops wobbling when she enters the same visual thought. The storm shift is not a new scene style; it is the same golden space losing confidence as grey creeps into the upper petals.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera mostly follows Fuzzby and struggles to keep up, letting him leave the frame edge for tiny breaths so his chaos feels larger than the lens. It does not wait safely for impacts; it discovers the leaf, pollen burst and flower trap with him. When Zenny’s judgement matters, the camera abandons his recovery and finds her stillness, making her look the punchline instead of adding an extra gag.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Fuzzby is constant motion against Zenny’s controlled economy. His hover never levels out; even in proud stance his wings and balance are working too hard. Zenny’s stillness is active thought: she watches, decides whether to smile, withholds it, then delivers the dry line. The first thunder rumble flips the contrast: Fuzzby’s motion goes crooked while Zenny becomes even more still, which makes the danger readable before she says it.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth is used as Fuzzby’s playground and trap. Foreground petals whip past, midground pollen clouds mark his route, background flowers sway like spectators. The leaf has weight and spring; it bends under him before firing him back. The moustache is born from contact with the environment, not from a random gag. By the end, depth closes down: the flower that traps him fills the space around him, while the storm-dark sky presses behind Zenny.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm begins as buoyant zig-zag music: Fuzzby’s “BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…” rides the movement. The leaf FWIP is the first punctuation. “Nailed it.” is a proud pause that arrives too soon. The moustache beat gives the audience time to read the status change before Zenny punctures it. The wipe-and-chain-reaction accelerates until “Buzz Crash!!” lands as a physical shout. Thunder then creates the first true gap in the tempo; Fuzzby tries to fill it with performance, Zenny names the real situation. The final pressure boast snaps the comedy back — and the flower swallows him before confidence can finish feeling safe.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by changed power or new comic information, never by coverage habit. Stay continuous through actions where momentum is the joke, especially the overcommitted dive and chain reaction. Cut cleanly to Zenny only when her stillness changes the meaning of Fuzzby’s movement. The storm gets one decisive tonal cut or reframing when the sound changes the sky and the relationship to danger; after that, the comedy button must arrive fast enough that the scene exits on character rather than weather exposition.
treatments.openingImage: A bee-scale corridor of tall rainforest flowers swaying in warm day light, pollen glittering in the air, with Fuzzby already pitched into a wild zig-zag streak through the space while Zenny, deeper in the flowers, completes one calm, precise pollen collection.
treatments.closingImage: Fuzzby stuck face-first in a flower after boasting about pressure, wings buzzing helplessly and pollen trembling loose, while Zenny holds nearby under the first greyed light of the coming storm — not panicked, just already tired because of course this is how it goes.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: I challenge the safe version where we open wide, place both bees neatly, then cover the gags from outside. That would make the field decorative and Fuzzby merely silly. The lens has to risk being wrong-footed by him: close enough for pollen to cross the lens path, low enough that stems tower, and mobile enough that Zenny’s stillness becomes a choice rather than a default locked frame.

treatments.name: Treatment 2 — Zenny’s Quiet Workday, Repeatedly Interrupted by a Tiny Parade
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience first feels the pleasure of calm competence: soft breeze, neat pollen gathering, a satisfying little rhythm. Then Fuzzby keeps invading that order like a marching band in a library. Children laugh at the contrast between smooth Zenny and crashy Fuzzby; adults enjoy the patience of someone who has seen this exact disaster in many costumes before.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Zenny’s experience governs the scene. She is trying to complete a simple task cleanly while sharing space with someone who needs an audience for every move. Her emotional truth is not irritation alone; it is practiced fondness. Fuzzby’s mask is transparent to her, so the scene’s warmth comes from the fact that she does not leave, even when she dryly names the absurdity.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary mechanism: movement against stillness. Fuzzby’s chaos crosses Zenny’s composed world and the hold on her processing is the joke. Secondary mechanism: deadpan observation. “Yes Fuzzby Officially nuts!” is not performed as a big punchline; it is the plainest possible report on the evidence. The storm turn works because Zenny’s stillness changes from comic judgement to real attention.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Zenny’s body carries the scene’s intelligence: exact paw placement, minimal wing correction, small eye movements before head turns, a near-smile rationed until Fuzzby’s moustache makes restraint difficult. She never competes with him for energy. Fuzzby plays maximum public ceremony: every pollen scoop is secretly an audition, every recovery becomes a chest-out presentation, every failed fix is disguised as intentional technique. When thunder arrives, Fuzzby tries to keep the show going; Zenny’s eyes go skyward before anything else moves.
treatments.visualGrammar: The scene is composed around calm frames that Fuzzby disrupts. The flower field has order from Zenny’s point of view: repeating stems, clear pollen targets, gentle sway. Fuzzby breaks those patterns with erratic altitude and diagonal entrances. The image language is less chase and more invasion: he passes through spaces that were balanced before he arrived. As the storm approaches, the same ordered verticals of stems begin to feel like a barometer, their tops darkening and leaning under heavier wind.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera often stays with Zenny’s task and lets Fuzzby enter unpredictably, sometimes as a blur, sometimes as a full proud presentation after the crash has already happened. It trusts the audience to reconstruct some impacts from aftermath because Zenny’s reaction is the meaning. The camera is not passive; it is allied with her patience, choosing when to give Fuzzby the stage and when to deny him the grandeur he thinks he has earned.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Stillness is the governing comic instrument. Zenny’s calm hover and controlled glides make Fuzzby’s every overcorrection louder. Fuzzby cannot share a frame without vibrating it; Zenny can change the whole scene with a slow blink. When thunder hits, the stillness is reclassified: what was a joke becomes awareness. Fuzzby keeps moving to avoid feeling the warning; Zenny stops because she has accepted it.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: The field is arranged as Zenny’s workspace: foreground pollen, reachable blossoms, a clear path from flower to flower. Fuzzby repeatedly collapses that order by knocking pollen into the air, bending a leaf into the path, and triggering a chain reaction that turns the workspace into a messy obstacle course. Depth carries Zenny’s vigilance: after the thunder, the darkening sky sits behind the upper petals where her attention has gone, while Fuzzby remains trapped in the immediate foreground nonsense.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The scene’s rhythm is built on interruptions. Begin with Zenny’s smooth, almost musical collecting pattern. Fuzzby’s “BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…” cuts across it and speeds the room up. The FWIP interrupts his own rhythm; “Nailed it.” attempts to restore status. The moustache beat slows down so Zenny’s withheld laugh can become the pressure point. The wipe gag breaks the quiet into a bigger tumble. Thunder then creates the longest clean silence of the scene, after which Fuzzby’s “...okay that sounded dramatic.” is a small attempt to reclaim the show. The final flower-stuck button returns the interruption pattern one last time.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts belong to Zenny’s attention. We cut when she notices a new category of Fuzzby trouble: noise, crash, moustache, worsening smear, storm. Avoid automatic impact/reaction coverage; sometimes the reaction is the only part we need, and sometimes Fuzzby’s re-entry with damage tells the missing impact more cleanly. Hold longer than usual on Zenny only when her processing is the punchline or the warning. Once the storm is named, cuts tighten so the scene does not become sentimental or explanatory.
treatments.openingImage: Zenny gliding through tall, warm rainforest flowers with calm precision, paws dusted gold as pollen trails settle neatly behind her; in the far depth, Fuzzby’s erratic buzzing line begins to scribble across the ordered space before he fully arrives.
treatments.closingImage: Zenny in a composed hover beneath darkening flower tops, looking toward the storm she has already understood, while Fuzzby remains half-swallowed by a blossom nearby — still trying to make pressure look like a plan.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: I challenge the assumption that a high-energy character requires a high-energy camera for the whole scene. If we chase Fuzzby constantly here, we lose Zenny’s comedy. The bolder choice is disciplined stillness that allows Fuzzby to vandalize the composition. But that stillness must be meaningful, not safe: frames must be built with enough depth and negative space for his interruptions to arrive as events.

treatments.name: Treatment 3 — The Flower Field Joins the Double Act
treatments.audienceExperience: The scene feels like the rainforest itself is playing with the bees. Flowers sway, petals offer pollen, leaves spring back, pollen clings, and the coming storm changes the rules. Children read a living playground that keeps boinging Fuzzby back; adults read a gentle world exposing the gap between performance and truth without cruelty.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The emotional point of view sits with the environment as witness and participant. Fuzzby wants to master the field; Zenny knows how to listen to it. The field does not punish him — it simply answers his force honestly. His need emerges because every leaf, petal and pollen cloud tells the truth his mouth will not: he is not in control, and he is still welcome in the game.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary mechanism: environmental participation. The leaf FWIPs, pollen creates the moustache, the wipe spreads it, flowers and stems pass the chain reaction along, thunder changes the air, and the final flower catches him. Secondary mechanism: anticipation to reversal. The field repeatedly appears to offer Fuzzby a grand entrance and instead delivers a soft, funny correction.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Fuzzby treats every part of the field as a prop in his personal ceremony. He dives into flowers as if entering a spotlight, recoils from leaves as if he meant to rebound, and uses posture to rename accidents as expertise. His body must show cause and effect: the leaf bends from his weight, pollen bursts from contact, the chain reaction travels from one overcommitted recovery. Zenny behaves like someone in partnership with the place: she follows the sway, times her glides to the breeze, takes only the pollen she needs, and notices the weather before Fuzzby can turn it into material.
treatments.visualGrammar: The visual grammar is tactile and cause-driven. Close environmental textures — pollen dust, petal rims, bending leaves, vibrating stems — are not inserts for prettiness; they are story actors. The camera sees the flowers as tall, soft mechanisms. Warm golden day light begins with floating pollen and soft green bounce; as thunder approaches, the upper canopy cools and the flower heads sway with a heavier rhythm. The scene remains playful, but the environment’s response grows firmer.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera sometimes belongs to the field rather than either bee: it may drift with a swaying stem, ride the recoil of a leaf, or discover Fuzzby as the thing that has just disturbed the pollen. With Zenny, the camera observes how little she needs to change the environment. With Fuzzby, it lets his force travel through the world. It never sits outside as a neutral recorder; it measures him by what he changes around him.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Movement is shared between character and place. Early flower sway is gentle and independent of the bees. Fuzzby introduces chaotic force that makes the field react: bent leaf, shaken pollen, jostled petals, chain reaction. Zenny moves within the existing rhythm rather than fighting it. When thunder arrives, the environment’s stillness tightens — a half-breath where petals pause before the wind shifts — and Zenny’s stillness matches it. Fuzzby is the only one still trying to perform through the change.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth is the main storytelling tool. Foreground leaves become springboards, midground flowers become Fuzzby’s mistaken targets, background flower tops reveal the weather change. Pollen suspended in layers shows where Fuzzby has been and how much mess he has made. The chain reaction should travel through depth so the field appears connected, not like isolated gag props. The final flower trap closes the depth around Fuzzby while the storm opens ominously above and beyond.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm begins with natural sway and soft pollen collection. Fuzzby’s chant adds a busy, self-authored rhythm over the field’s calmer pulse. Each environmental answer is sharper: soft pollen scoop, springy FWIP, sticky moustache, smeared correction, tumbling chain, thunder rumble, final petal catch. The escalation is not random; it is the field responding more visibly to Fuzzby’s refusal to reduce force. The storm is the first response not caused by him, which makes it dramatically different and gives Zenny’s warning weight.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by physical causality in the environment. If Fuzzby hits a leaf, we stay long enough to feel the bend and recoil. If pollen clings, we cut or reframe when the new information becomes legible as moustache. If the chain reaction travels, the editorial logic follows the transfer of force from stem to petal to bee. The thunder cut is motivated by a change in the whole field’s behaviour, not just a sound cue. Avoid isolated gag coverage; every cut should prove how the world participates.
treatments.openingImage: A towering rainforest flower bends gently in warm daylight, its petal cup full of golden pollen; Zenny’s careful paw gathers from one side in rhythm with the sway as Fuzzby’s buzzing path rattles the pollen from the other side before he bursts fully into view.
treatments.closingImage: A flower that has become a soft trap holds Fuzzby after his pressure boast, its petals quivering from the impact; beyond him, layered flower tops tilt under a greyer sky while Zenny hovers in the weather’s rhythm, already listening to what the field is saying.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: I challenge any plan that treats leaves and flowers as background dressing around bee business. In this treatment, the environment is the third performer. The camera must prove weight, contact and consequence in the materials — bending, dusting, springing, clamping — or the comedy becomes weightless posing. The risk is letting tactile environmental causality drive the scene instead of relying on familiar character coverage.

treatmentSelection.selectedTreatment: Treatment 1 led, fused with Treatment 3’s tactile flower-field causality
combinedFrom: Treatment 1 — Fuzzby’s Grand Flight That the World Keeps Correcting
Treatment 3 — The Flower Field Joins the Double Act
treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: The audience rides inside Fuzzby’s overconfident zoom as the flower field keeps telling the truth his mouth won’t, until Zenny’s stillness and the first storm-darkening turn the laugh into a tiny gulp.
treatmentSelection.rationale: Treatment 1 has the correct emotional engine for the scene: Fuzzby’s bravado is the point, Zenny’s witness gives it warmth, and the comedy plants the episode’s courage/bravado theme without explaining it. It also gives the camera a lived relationship to Fuzzby’s momentum rather than merely recording gags. Treatment 3 supplies the most memorable visual opportunity: the rainforest is not decoration but a soft, reactive physical world, so every laugh has cause, contact and consequence. Combined, they make the scene specific to Crystal Bears: a bright play-space where feeling is externalised through body, pollen, leaf-spring, weather shift and a friend who sees the truth and stays. Treatment 2 contributes a useful reminder that Zenny’s stillness must be charged, but as the governing approach it shifts the scene too far into her workday and risks making Fuzzby’s first thesis-beat feel like interruption comedy instead of the episode’s opening statement about performed confidence.
treatmentSelection.rejectionChecks: Reject Treatment 2 as the standalone governing treatment: it leans too heavily on Zenny-held compositions and interruption/reaction logic, which risks safe camera placement and habitual action/reaction coverage even though its stillness idea is valuable. Do not carry forward any fixed character lanes, any requirement to keep both characters visible, any repeated close-up punctuation after each gag, or any mechanical shot-count thinking. Reject any version of Treatment 1 that becomes simple chase coverage or merely illustrates Fuzzby’s crashes from outside. Reject any version of Treatment 3 that makes the environment the emotional centre and weakens the Fuzzby/Zenny relationship. The selected approach must keep cinematography as co-author: the camera is wrong-footed by Fuzzby, calmed by Zenny, and convinced by the physical field, with cuts motivated by changed meaning or transferred force rather than coverage habit.

scene.purpose: Open the episode at bee scale by making Fuzzby’s performed confidence, Zenny’s calm witness, and the reactive flower field instantly legible before the first storm warning bends the comedy toward courage.
scene.dramaticQuestion: Can Fuzzby keep selling himself as masterful when the flowers, pollen, leaf-spring and thunder keep revealing the opposite?
scene.connectionFromPreviousScene: Episode opening: the audience enters already in motion, inside Fuzzby’s overconfident pollen run, with Zenny’s precision nearby as contrast.
scene.handoverToNextScene: Fuzzby is physically stuck after boasting, the first storm-darkening is established, and Zenny’s steady attention carries the warning forward without panic.

beats.sourceScript: The episode opens at bee scale in a bright flower field: Zenny’s graceful competence and Fuzzby’s chaotic overconfidence are instantly legible. Fuzzby’s first pollen dive becomes a crash he rebrands as mastery, planting the whole episode’s comic idea that bravado is not the same as courage.

orderedEvents.text: Tall flowers sway gently in the warm breeze. Some stretch high above the grass, with long soft necks and bright open petals full of pollen. FUZZBY and ZENNY weave between them collecting pollen from flower to flower. Fine golden pollen dusts their paws and trails softly through the air. Zenny works with smooth calm precision — neat, efficient, graceful. Fuzzby does not. He zig-zags wildly through the air, humming loudly to himself as he works.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…
He dips low into a flower, scoops up pollen — then overdoes it and spins sideways into a leaf. FWIP. He bounces back into the air and straightens up proudly.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: Nailed it.
Zenny glides up beside him. Watches him for a beat.

beats.whatChanges: A warm flower field turns from simple pollen work into a character thesis: Zenny’s quiet competence reads cleanly while Fuzzby’s first attempt at mastery physically disproves him.
beats.whoDrives: Fuzzby drives the change with speed, volume and overcommitment; the leaf and pollen supply the correction, and Zenny’s precision supplies the contrast.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience is invited to enjoy the fast bee-scale ride and anticipate that Fuzzby’s confidence is arriving one mistake before his body can support it.
beats.actionOrChoice: Fuzzby zig-zags through the flowers, sings his work rhythm, dives low to scoop pollen, overdoes the move, spins sideways into a leaf, bounces back and chooses pride before balance has fully returned.
beats.consequence: The flower field has already told on him: the leaf’s spring and his proud recovery make his “mastery” visibly ridiculous, with pollen and wobbling recovery still present as evidence.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The beat hands over a playable rule for the scene: Fuzzby will rebrand every crash as competence, and the world will keep answering in soft physical truth.

emotionContract.entryState: Already launched into bright, noisy certainty, working hard to look impressive while collecting pollen.
emotionContract.pressure: Zenny’s smooth pollen work is nearby, and the giant flower field demands precision that his speed does not provide.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: He chooses to treat the leaf bounce as proof of skill instead of letting the crash register as a mistake.
emotionContract.exitState: Proud but physically betrayed: straightened up, still carrying the evidence of the bounce and the overdone dive.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: His zig-zag line, loud work chant, sideways spin into the leaf, rebound and too-fast proud stance make the gap between claim and body readable.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience now knows the flowers will correct Fuzzby before Fuzzby admits anything.

comedyContract.setup: Two bees collect pollen in a tall flower field: Zenny works neatly while Fuzzby attacks the same job like a grand performance.
comedyContract.expectation: His loud rhythm and fast dive promise impressive efficiency.
comedyContract.disruption: He overdoes the scoop, spins sideways into a leaf, and the leaf springs him back like the field has edited his performance.
comedyContract.hold: Hold long enough after the line for his proud pose and unstable recovery to contradict each other before moving on.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: Keep Fuzzby’s approach path, the pollen scoop, the leaf contact, the leaf bend and the rebound consequence readable as one chain; Zenny’s calmer work remains available as contrast, not coverage obligation.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: Fuzzby’s momentum carries into the leaf; the leaf visibly bends under his small weight, stores the force, then releases him back into the air with pollen trailing from the contact.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: A confident diagonal dive becomes a sideways skid, a spring-back, then an over-proud upright recovery that arrives before his balance does.
prohibitedStaging: Do not make the leaf bounce feel weightless or magical; the bend must cause the FWIP.
Do not cut away before contact and recoil have completed their cause-and-effect.
Do not play Fuzzby as calmly skilled before the crash; his overcommitment is the cause.

beats.sourceScript: Fuzzby escalates from pollen collector to self-appointed official by accidentally wearing a pollen moustache. Zenny’s almost-withheld laugh and dry tease make the relationship the punchline: she sees exactly who he is and stays beside him anyway.

orderedEvents.text: He zooms to another flower, humming louder, and sticks his whole face into it. A beat. He pulls back out completely dusted in pollen like a fuzzy yellow moustache. Zenny tries not to laugh.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: Do I look official?

orderedEvents.speaker: Zenny
orderedEvents.text: Yes Fuzzby Officially nuts!

beats.whatChanges: The pollen accident becomes a status costume: Fuzzby stops being merely a messy worker and appoints himself important because the moustache lets him pretend the mess means rank.
beats.whoDrives: Fuzzby drives the status claim; Zenny changes the meaning by withholding, then delivering, the dry puncture.
beats.audienceAnticipation: Children anticipate whether the moustache will make him proud or embarrassed; adults anticipate Zenny seeing the performance exactly and choosing the smallest possible pin.
beats.actionOrChoice: Fuzzby notices the accidental pollen moustache and asks for official recognition instead of wiping it away; Zenny chooses a contained tease rather than rescuing him from the joke.
beats.consequence: The relationship locks in: he performs importance, she names the nonsense, and neither leaves the other alone in it.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The moustache tease hands into the next beat as a physical problem Fuzzby cannot leave alone, priming the wipe that will worsen everything.

emotionContract.entryState: Fresh from a proud recovery and eager to convert visible mess into proof that he matters.
emotionContract.pressure: The pollen moustache is obvious, Zenny is watching, and the field has just made him look less competent than he wants.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: He chooses status over embarrassment by asking if he looks official.
emotionContract.exitState: Momentarily elevated by his own idea, then exposed by Zenny’s exact, affectionate puncture.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: He presents the pollen moustache as if it were an earned badge; Zenny’s held look and dry answer land against his inflated posture.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience holds both truths: Fuzzby wants the mess to count as importance, and Zenny’s tease keeps him included rather than rejected.

comedyContract.mechanism: Status change through concealment to revelation, capped by deadpan observation.
comedyContract.setup: Fuzzby’s crash leaves pollen arranged as a moustache, giving him an accidental new look.
comedyContract.expectation: He will notice the mess and either be embarrassed or try to fix it.
comedyContract.disruption: He promotes the mess into authority and asks for confirmation.
comedyContract.hold: Let Zenny’s almost-smile and flat delivery sit just long enough for the audience to see her affection under the tease.

beats.sourceScript: Fuzzby tries to fix the moustache and only makes it worse, then turns the whole field into a chain-reaction tumble. The gag escalates through overcommitment: every attempt to recover becomes a bigger physical confession of failure.

orderedEvents.text: Fuzzby gasps. He wipes at his face. Somehow smears the pollen worse. He dives again toward another flower — clips a branch — tumbles end over end through the air. THUP. THUP. THUP. He lands upside down inside a blossom. Beat. His little legs kick. Then he pops back up.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: Buzz Crash!!
Zenny rolls her eyes, but she is smiling now. Fuzzby hums louder and dives into another flower. He pops back out, somehow even more covered in pollen than before.

beats.whatChanges: A small face mess becomes a full-field chain reaction; Fuzzby’s attempt to repair dignity proves the larger confession that he cannot control his own momentum.
beats.whoDrives: Fuzzby drives every escalation by trying to fix and recover too hard; the flowers, pollen and stems convert that effort into visible consequences.

showrunnerJudgement: PASS. I tried to reject this for safe coverage, reaction-shot habit, and loss of the selected ride-inside-Fuzzby experience, but the scene holds its governing idea. The storyboard keeps Fuzzby’s body as the argument and the flower field as the truth-teller: speed, overcommitment, environmental correction, proud verbal cover, then Zenny’s stillness as the comic pin. The storm turn also remains inside the same comic grammar rather than becoming a separate weather-exposition scene. This feels like Crystal Bears because the joke is relationship-shaped: Fuzzby needs to be impressive; Zenny sees the mess and stays.
treatmentComparison: Against Treatment 1, this is a faithful whole-scene translation. The opening is not a neutral establishing shot; it launches already in Fuzzby’s motion. The camera is instructed to struggle with him, discover impacts with him, and cut to Zenny only when her stillness changes the meaning. The comic mechanism remains escalating overcommitment: leaf rebound, moustache, smear, chain reaction, thunder cover, pressure boast, flower trap. The audience experience is preserved: children get the fast bee-scale ride and repeated physical comeuppance; adults get the tiny performer trying to look official while his own body keeps confessing. The thunder beat correctly shaves warmth off the laughter without stopping the comedy, and the closing image lands on character embarrassment under newly grey light rather than on generic storm danger.

The split is not an empty join: it protects both duration and dramatic complexity, with SH1 carrying the launch/status-moustache setup and SH2 carrying the fix-escalation, tonal thunder turn, and flower-trap payoff. Each unit stays within the stated stage/internal-shot limits, and the split occurs at a real story handoff: the moustache stops being a badge and becomes the problem Fuzzby cannot leave alone.
